_note: member-onboarding-in-plain-words — a traject is a pathway, and joining or leaving a governance body is a pathway every organisation walks. The-last-two-dutch-names claimed decidiq shipped no Dutch-named schema outside the Woo plumbing; these two were still here, and their descriptions were written for a griffie and a raadswisseling. Renamed to MemberOnboarding and MemberOffboarding, with the Dutch property beëdigingsType and the two swearing-in names renamed with them, and three council vocabularies freed to be free text. Updated by plain-words-for-groups-and-the-installation-step: the notification recipient group is now decidiq-secretariat, and the swearing-in step type is now installation.

MemberOnboarding.title: Member onboarding
MemberOnboarding.description: Everything one person has to go through to take up a place on a governance body, held as data: who is joining, which body, in which role, the checklist of steps and where each one stands, and the installation once it has happened. Renamed from OnboardingTraject (member-onboarding-in-plain-words). A council installs a new member, a board admits a director, an association welcomes a committee member: it is the same record, and only the word was Dutch. Everything it references (Membership, groups, meetings) is owned elsewhere and linked by UUID; this schema creates none of them. Declarative core only: account provisioning and induction-pack delivery stay imperative side effects elsewhere. The manifest and every widget source reference this schema by its slug 'member-onboarding'.
MemberOnboarding._authorizationNote: NEW BLOCK, NOT INHERITED, and that is deliberate. OnboardingTraject and OffboardingTraject declared no authorization of their own, so their rule came from the decidiq register baseline, which lists `public` among both readers and listers. These records carry a person's name, their account id, when they were installed and why they left, including reasons such as death and relocation. That was readable and listable by anonymous visitors and nothing reported it, the same defect conflict-of-interest-authorization-guard fixed for ConflictOfInterest. `read` and `list` are BOTH declared: a schema block shadows the register baseline, and leaving `list` unstated would leave its resolution to a fallback this repository does not own. `list` is a canonical action in OpenRegister's PermissionHandler. No write action is declared, so create, update and delete stay on the baseline.

x-openregister-lifecycle._note: COMPLETION GUARD (REQ-MOB-003): an onboarding must NOT reach 'completed' while any mandatory step is not 'completed'. `completed` and `lapsed` are terminal.

memberOnboardingCreated._note: Created notification to the secretariat group (REQ-MOB-010). The dialect has no recipient kind that targets the {{person}}'s account directly; object-acl(read) plus decidiq-secretariat and decidesk-members is the closest declarative approximation, and it is never an imperative send.

onboardingStepDueSoon._note: Due-soon step rappel (REQ-MOB-010). intervalSec 86400 (daily) is PROVISIONAL. Filter targets non-terminal lifecycle only. The 'a step's dueDate is approaching' vs 'a step is past its dueDate' distinction lives inside the steps array; the simple filter shape cannot express a per-step dueDate comparison — verify OR's scheduled-notification engine interprets this and onboardingStepOverdue as due-soon/overdue window semantics at live import (same caveat as the toezegging rappels).

onboardingStepOverdue._note: Overdue step rappel (REQ-MOB-010). intervalSec 86400 (daily) is PROVISIONAL. Filters non-terminal lifecycle so nothing fires for completed or lapsed records. Same per-step-dueDate window caveat as onboardingStepDueSoon.

person.title: Person
person.description: Reference to the incoming member's Person (schema:Action object). Required.

targetBody.title: Target body
targetBody.description: Reference to the governance body the person is joining. Required. With targetRole it derives the body-role group mapping the assign-groups step uses.

targetRole.title: Target role
targetRole.description: The role the member takes up (matches the Membership role enum, person-and-membership). Required.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: What set this off: one person joining, a whole intake at once, or someone stepping in mid-term. Free text, because what an organisation calls its intake is its own vocabulary.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The onboarding checklist. Required. Each step carries its own status. The work behind account-linking, assign-groups and induction-pack happens elsewhere; this array records that the step exists and where it stands.

stepType.title: Step type
stepType.description: What kind of step this is. `custom` is a step the organisation defined itself.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the step stands. A step may only be `skipped` when mandatory is false, enforced at save time.

mandatory.title: Mandatory
mandatory.description: Whether the step is mandatory. A mandatory step blocks the onboarding from reaching `completed` until it is `completed` itself.

dueDate.title: Due date
dueDate.description: Optional date the step is due. Drives the declarative due-soon and overdue step reminders and the overdue-steps dashboard KPI.

completedAt.title: Completed at
completedAt.description: Set when the step is completed.

completedBy.title: Completed by
completedBy.description: Nextcloud UID of the person who completed the step.

note.title: Note
note.description: Optional free-text note on the step (e.g. a skip reason or a provisioning result).

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: Optional object UUID linking what the step is about: the meeting where the person was installed, the induction pack that was delivered, the membership that was created.

installedOn.title: Oath date
installedOn.description: Date the person was formally installed. Completing the installation step requires this, installationType and installationMeeting.

installationType.title: Oath type
installationType.description: How the person was formally installed, where the organisation marks that at all. Free text: a council takes an oath or an affirmation, a board signs a deed, an association records a vote, and none of those is every organisation's word.

installationMeeting.title: Oath meeting
installationMeeting.description: Reference to the Meeting where the person was installed. The meeting itself is owned elsewhere and only linked here.

ncAccount.title: Nextcloud account
ncAccount.description: Nextcloud user id linked to the person by the account-linking step. Optional until linked; the induction-pack step depends on it.

membership.title: Membership
membership.description: Reference to the Membership created as an outcome. Optional until created: an intake often onboards a person before the membership row exists.

batch.title: Batch
batch.description: Free-form label linking the records created by one intake run. Optional; drives the batch filter on the index.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Where the onboarding stands. Declared in x-openregister-lifecycle (ADR-031): started, in-execution, then completed or lapsed.

MemberOffboarding.title: Member offboarding
MemberOffboarding.description: Everything one person has to go through to leave a governance body, held as data: who is leaving, which body, which membership ends and when, why it ends, the checklist of steps and where each one stands, and the confirmation. Renamed from OffboardingTraject (member-onboarding-in-plain-words). The checklist always includes end-dating the membership, withdrawing the account's groups and access, a personal-data note pointing at the author export, and the exit confirmation. Declarative core only: revoking access and end-dating the membership stay imperative side effects elsewhere. The manifest and every widget source reference this schema by its slug 'member-offboarding'.
MemberOffboarding._authorizationNote: NEW BLOCK, NOT INHERITED, and that is deliberate. OnboardingTraject and OffboardingTraject declared no authorization of their own, so their rule came from the decidiq register baseline, which lists `public` among both readers and listers. These records carry a person's name, their account id, when they were installed and why they left, including reasons such as death and relocation. That was readable and listable by anonymous visitors and nothing reported it, the same defect conflict-of-interest-authorization-guard fixed for ConflictOfInterest. `read` and `list` are BOTH declared: a schema block shadows the register baseline, and leaving `list` unstated would leave its resolution to a fallback this repository does not own. `list` is a canonical action in OpenRegister's PermissionHandler. No write action is declared, so create, update and delete stay on the baseline.

x-openregister-lifecycle._note: COMPLETION GUARD: an offboarding must NOT reach 'completed' while any mandatory step is not 'completed'; the revoke-groups step is ALWAYS mandatory, so access is never left standing behind a finished record.

memberOffboardingCreated._note: Created notification to the secretariat group (REQ-MOB-010). object-acl(read) plus decidiq-secretariat and decidesk-members is the closest declarative approximation, and it is never an imperative send.

offboardingStepDueSoon._note: Due-soon step rappel (REQ-MOB-010). intervalSec 86400 (daily) is PROVISIONAL. Filters non-terminal lifecycle. Per-step dueDate window semantics: verify against OR's scheduled-notification engine at live import (same caveat as the onboarding rappels).

offboardingStepOverdue._note: Overdue step rappel (REQ-MOB-010). intervalSec 86400 (daily) is PROVISIONAL. Filters non-terminal lifecycle. Same per-step-dueDate window caveat as offboardingStepDueSoon.

person.title: Person
person.description: Reference to the departing member's Person (schema:Action object). Required.

body.title: Body
body.description: Reference to the governance body the person is leaving. Required. With the person's role it derives the body-role group mapping the revoke-groups step uses.

membership.title: Membership
membership.description: Reference to the Membership to be end-dated. Required. End-dating happens on the end-membership step, never as an automatic side effect.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: What set this off: one person leaving, or a whole turnover at once. Free text, because what an organisation calls its turnover is its own vocabulary.

endDate.title: End date
endDate.description: Date the membership ends. The end-membership step sets Membership.endDate to this value.

endReason.title: End reason
endReason.description: Why the membership ends. Free text: end of term, resignation, relocation, death, or whatever else an organisation records.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The offboarding checklist. Required. Includes at minimum end-membership, revoke-groups (always mandatory), a personal-data note and the exit confirmation.

stepType.title: Step type
stepType.description: What kind of step this is. `personal-data-note` points at the author export rather than repeating it; `custom` is a step the organisation defined itself.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the step stands. A step may only be `skipped` when mandatory is false, enforced at save time. The revoke-groups step is always mandatory and can never be skipped.

mandatory.title: Mandatory
mandatory.description: Whether the step is mandatory. A mandatory step blocks the offboarding from reaching `completed` until it is `completed` itself; revoke-groups is always mandatory.

dueDate.title: Due date
dueDate.description: Optional date the step is due. Drives the declarative due-soon and overdue step reminders and the overdue-steps dashboard KPI.

completedAt.title: Completed at
completedAt.description: Set when the step is completed.

completedBy.title: Completed by
completedBy.description: Nextcloud UID of the person who completed the step.

note.title: Note
note.description: Optional free-text note (e.g. the verified post-revocation group list, or a skip reason).

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: Optional URL or object UUID linking the step's subject (e.g. the document-annotations export for the persoonsgegevens-notitie step).

exitConfirmedBy.title: Exit confirmed by
exitConfirmedBy.description: Account id of the person who confirmed the exit. Optional until confirmed.

exitConfirmedOn.title: Exit confirmed at
exitConfirmedOn.description: When the exit was confirmed. Optional until confirmed.

batch.title: Batch
batch.description: Free-form label linking the records created by one turnover run. Optional; drives the batch filter on the index.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Where the offboarding stands. Declared in x-openregister-lifecycle (ADR-031): started, in-execution, then completed or lapsed. It cannot reach completed while the always-mandatory revoke-groups step is not completed.

OnboardingTraject.description: SUPERSEDED (member-onboarding-in-plain-words): the same thing as MemberOnboarding (slug member-onboarding). Definition and slug are kept (hardDelete:false, existing rows).

OffboardingTraject.description: SUPERSEDED (member-onboarding-in-plain-words): the same thing as MemberOffboarding (slug member-offboarding). Definition and slug are kept (hardDelete:false, existing rows).
